i18n.en: The oracle concerning Tyre. Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in; from the land of Kittim it is revealed to them.
i18n.he: מַשָּׂ֖א צֹ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ ׀ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־שֻׁדַּ֤ד מִבַּ֙יִת֙ מִבּ֔וֹא מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כִּתִּ֖ים נִגְלָה־לָֽמוֹ׃

notes.official:
*Maśśāʾ ṣōr* “The oracle concerning Tyre” uses the heading formula of 13:1 and 15:1 (overlay `massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah`). ASV and JPS 1917 have “The burden of Tyre”; NJPS has “The ‘Tyre’ Pronouncement.” *Hêlîlû ʾŏniyyôṯ taršîš* “Wail, O ships of Tarshish” repeats the phrase of 2:16 (wave I-4 ruling 8), and the summons returns at 23:14 to frame the poem. *Hêlîlû* is “wail” at 23:1, 6 and 14, as at 13:6 and 14:31. ASV has “howl” at 23:1 and 14 and “wail” at 23:6, and NJPS has “howl” throughout.

*Kî-šuddad mibbayiṯ mibbôʾ* is elliptical. The line reads the two *min*-phrases as privative, “so that there is no house, no entering in,” with ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS reads “not a house is left” and joins *mibbôʾ* to the next clause: “As they came from the land of Kittim, This was revealed to them.” *Bôʾ* may mean the entering of a harbor, a sense some modern versions make explicit. *Kittîm* takes the ASV spelling. The name goes back to Kition on Cyprus and usually refers to Cyprus; the identification is given here and kept out of the line (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`). In *niḡlāh-lāmô* “it is revealed to them,” the ships hear the news on their way home.

notes.official:
*Dōmmû* “Be still”: ASV and JPS 1917 read *dmm* I “be silent, be still.” NJPS has “Moan,” which takes the verb as a homonym meaning “wail, lament.” The lexica propose such a homonym, but their entries were not checked here. The line keeps the public-domain reading. The alternative would fit the calls to wail in 23:1 and 23:6. *Yōšᵉḇê ʾî* is “inhabitants of the coastland.” The book renders *ʾî / ʾiyyîm* “coastland(s)” (11:11; 24:15; 40:15; 20:6; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-11`). ASV has “the coast,” JPS 1917 “coast-land” and NJPS “coastland dwellers.” The word covers both the island city of Tyre and the Phoenician coast.

The second half follows MT. *Sōḥēr ṣîḏôn ʿōḇēr yām millᵉʾûḵ* has a singular collective “merchant,” a plural verb and a second-person feminine singular suffix: “(you whom) the merchants of Sidon, crossing the sea, have filled.” ASV and JPS 1917 read it the same way (“have replenished”). NJPS construes MT differently: “You traders of Sidon, Once thronged by seafarers.” For *millᵉʾûḵ*, the Great Isaiah Scroll reads *mlʾkyk* “your messengers.” This is reported in an online collation of 1QIsaᵃ col. XVIII (Fred P. Miller, *The Great Isaiah Scroll*, ao.net/~fmoeller), but the reading was not checked against DJD 32 or the scroll images. NRSV follows it with “your messengers crossed over the sea” (recalled, not verified). The line follows MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

notes.official:
*Qᵉṣîr yᵉʾôr* “the harvest of the Nile”: *yᵉʾôr* is the Egyptian loanword for the Nile (Egyptian *itrw*; central `yeor-nile-egyptian-loanword`). The central entry's default is “the river,” which is ASV's word in Genesis 41. In Isaiah, however, ASV prints “the Nile” for singular *yᵉʾôr* (19:7, 8; 23:3, 10; checked). JPS 1917 and NJPS also have “the Nile” here. The parallel phrase *zeraʿ šiḥōr* “the seed of Shihor” names water on Egypt's border. This wave adds an Isaiah context clause to the central entry: singular *yᵉʾôr* is “the Nile.” The clause also keeps *yᵉʾôr* apart from *nāhār* “the River,” which the book uses for the Euphrates (7:20; 8:7; 11:15; 27:12). The plural stays “rivers” (7:18).

*Šiḥōr* has no article in MT, and the line follows JPS 1917 and NJPS “Shihor” against ASV “the Shihor.” The name is Egyptian and is usually taken as a Nile branch or lake on Egypt's eastern border (Josh 13:3; Jer 2:18); the etymology was not verified. *Sᵉḥar gôyim* is “the market of nations,” the modern English for ASV and JPS 1917 “the mart of nations.” *Sᵉḥar* is both the trader's gain and the place of trade, and NJPS takes it as a source of revenue: “From the trade of nations.” The grain of Egypt reached Tyre *ûḇᵉmayim rabbîm* “on great waters,” by sea (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`).

paragraphs.translit: ūbəmayim rabbīm zeraʿ šiḥōr qəṣīr yəʾōr təbūʾātāh wattəhī səḥar gōyim

paragraphs.text: בּ֣וֹשִׁי צִיד֔וֹן כִּֽי־אָמַ֣ר יָ֔ם מָע֥וֹז הַיָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־חַ֣לְתִּי וְלֹֽא־יָלַ֗דְתִּי וְלֹ֥א גִדַּ֛לְתִּי בַּחוּרִ֖ים רוֹמַ֥מְתִּי בְתוּלֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Be ashamed, O Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying: “I have not been in labor, nor given birth; I have not reared young men, nor brought up virgins.”
i18n.he: בּ֣וֹשִׁי צִיד֔וֹן כִּֽי־אָמַ֣ר יָ֔ם מָע֥וֹז הַיָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־חַ֣לְתִּי וְלֹֽא־יָלַ֗דְתִּי וְלֹ֥א גִדַּ֛לְתִּי בַּחוּרִ֖ים רוֹמַ֥מְתִּי בְתוּלֽוֹת׃

notes.official: *Bôšî ṣîḏôn* “Be ashamed, O Sidon”: Sidon stands for Phoenicia as a whole. In *yām … māʿôz hayyām* “the sea …, the stronghold of the sea,” the second phrase may be the sea itself or Tyre, the island fortress. The line keeps the Hebrew apposition with ASV and JPS 1917. The sea speaks as a woman who has borne no children. *Lōʾ-ḥaltî wᵉlōʾ-yālaḏtî* “I have not been in labor, nor given birth” puts ASV's “travailed … brought forth” into modern English. NJPS renders “I am as one who has never labored,” with a note that the Hebrew has “I have.” *Bᵉṯûlôṯ* is “virgins” with ASV and JPS 1917, paired with *baḥûrîm* “young men”; NJPS has “maidens.” The same noun forms the title “virgin daughter of Sidon” at 23:12 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`). The speech is in quotation marks, as in JPS 1917 and NJPS (overlay `title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: bōšī ṣīdōn kī-ʾāmar yām māʿōz hayyām lēʾmōr lōʾ-ḥaltī wəlōʾ-yāladtī wəlōʾ giddaltī baḥūrīm rōmamtī bətūlōt

i18n.en: When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report of Tyre.

notes.official: *Kaʾăšer šēmaʿ lᵉmiṣrāyim yāḥîlû kᵉšēmaʿ ṣōr* is compressed. The line reads *kaʾăšer* as temporal with ASV and JPS 1917: “When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report of Tyre.” KJV reads a comparison: “As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre” (checked). NJPS makes the Egyptians the hearers: “When the Egyptians heard it, they quailed As when they heard about Tyre.” *Yāḥîlû* (*ḥyl* “writhe, be in anguish”) carries on the birth imagery of 23:4. “Egypt” takes the English form under the wave rulings (overlay `aram-names-isaiah`).

i18n.en: Cross over to Tarshish; wail, inhabitants of the coastland!

notes.official: *ʿIḇrû taršîšāh* “Cross over to Tarshish” (ASV “Pass ye over”) sends the refugees west to the distant colony. The verb *ʿbr* runs through the chapter: “crossing the sea” (23:2), “pass through your land” (23:10), “cross over to Kittim” (23:12). The English varies with the construction, and each rendering is ASV's. *Hêlîlû* is “wail,” as at 23:1 and 23:14, and *yōšᵉḇê ʾî* is “inhabitants of the coastland,” as at 23:2 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-11`).

paragraphs.text: הֲזֹ֥את לָכֶ֖ם עַלִּיזָ֑ה מִֽימֵי־קֶ֤דֶם קַדְמָתָהּ֙ יֹבִל֣וּהָ רַגְלֶ֔יהָ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לָגֽוּר׃

i18n.en: Is this your jubilant city, whose antiquity is from days of old, whose feet carried her far off to sojourn?
i18n.he: הֲזֹ֥את לָכֶ֖ם עַלִּיזָ֑ה מִֽימֵי־קֶ֤דֶם קַדְמָתָהּ֙ יֹבִל֣וּהָ רַגְלֶ֔יהָ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לָגֽוּר׃

notes.official: *Hăzōʾṯ lāḵem ʿallîzāh* “Is this your jubilant city”: the adjective *ʿallîzāh* has no noun, and the line supplies “city,” which ASV marks as supplied (“joyous [city]”). The same adjective is “jubilant” in *ʿîr ʿallîzāh* “the jubilant city” at the stable 32:13 and in *qiryāh ʿallîzāh* at 22:2. Its root gives the infinitive “exult” at 23:12, and “rejoice” stays with *śmḥ* (14:29) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`). *Mîmê-qeḏem qaḏmāṯāh* “whose antiquity is from days of old” follows ASV's construal. *Yōḇilûhā raḡleyhā mērāḥôq lāḡûr* “whose feet carried her far off to sojourn” has an imperfect verb. It may describe past habit, the colonies Tyre founded far away, or a future exile. NJPS makes it a question about the past: “Did her feet carry her off To sojourn far away?”

paragraphs.translit: hăzōʾt lākem ʿallīzāh mīmē-qedem qadmātāh yōbilūhā raglēhā mērāḥōq lāgūr

paragraphs.text: מִ֚י יָעַ֣ץ זֹ֔את עַל־צֹ֖ר הַמַּֽעֲטִירָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר סֹחֲרֶ֙יה֙ שָׂרִ֔ים כִּנְעָנֶ֖יהָ נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Who has planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the honored of the earth?
i18n.he: מִ֚י יָעַ֣ץ זֹ֔את עַל־צֹ֖ר הַמַּֽעֲטִירָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר סֹחֲרֶ֙יה֙ שָׂרִ֔ים כִּנְעָנֶ֖יהָ נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official: *Hammaʿăṭîrāh* is a Hiphil participle of *ʿṭr* “surround, crown.” ASV reads it as transitive, “the bestower of crowns,” Tyre as the city that crowned the kings of its colonies. JPS 1917 reads “the crowning city” and NJPS “crown-wearing Tyre.” The line keeps ASV. *Kinʿāneyhā*, literally “her Canaanites,” means “her traders,” as at Hos 12:8 (Eng. 12:7) and Prov 31:24. ASV and JPS 1917 have “traffickers” and NJPS “traders.” *Niḵbaddê-ʾāreṣ* “the honored of the earth” is the Niphal participle of *kbd*, as in “you are honored” at 43:4. ASV and JPS 1917 have “honorable,” and NJPS has “Whose traders the world honored.” The participle is not the noun *kāḇôḏ*, so the strict “glory” rule (wave I-4 ruling 2) does not apply. Nor does it use the noun “honor” fixed for *tip̄ʾereṯ*, since it is a verbal form. *Yāʿaṣ* “has planned” (ASV “purposed”) prepares the answer in 23:9 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`).

paragraphs.translit: mī yāʿaṣ zōʾt ʿal-ṣōr hammaʿăṭīrāh ʾăšer sōḥărēh śārīm kinʿānēhā nikbaddē-ʾāreṣ

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יְעָצָ֑הּ לְחַלֵּל֙ גְּא֣וֹן כָּל־צְבִ֔י לְהָקֵ֖ל כָּל־נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: YHWH of hosts has planned it, to profane the pride of all beauty, to bring into contempt all the honored of the earth.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יְעָצָ֑הּ לְחַלֵּל֙ גְּא֣וֹן כָּל־צְבִ֔י לְהָקֵ֖ל כָּל־נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official:
*Lᵉḥallēl gᵉʾôn kol-ṣᵉḇî* “to profane the pride of all beauty”: the line departs from ASV and JPS 1917 (“the pride of all glory”) in one word. *Ṣᵉḇî* means “beauty, ornament” (BDB; HALOT; recalled), and NJPS renders the phrase “all glorious beauty.” Wave I-4 ruling 2 keeps “glory” for *kāḇôḏ*. The stable 4:2 already renders *ṣᵉḇî* “beauty” next to *kāḇôḏ* “glory,” and that decision is extended here (overlay `tsevi-beauty-isaiah`). By founder ruling of 2026-11-26 the stable 13:19 now reads “the beauty of kingdoms,” and 24:16 “Glory to the righteous one!” is recorded as an idiomatic departure, where the noun is the content of an acclamation.

*Gāʾôn* is “pride” rather than the book's default “majesty” (2:10; 24:14; overlay `hadar-splendor-isaiah`). Here the word names a human self-exaltation that YHWH profanes. The stable 13:19 (“the pride of the Chaldeans”) and 16:6 render that sense “pride”, and the recorded departure under wave I-4 ruling 2 is governed by overlay `gaon-pride-human-arrogance-isaiah`. *Lᵉḥallēl* (Piel of *ḥll* “treat as common, defile”) is “to profane”; ASV has “stain,” JPS 1917 “pollute” and NJPS “defile.” *Lᵉhāqēl* (Hiphil of *qll* “be light”) is “to bring into contempt” with ASV and JPS 1917; NJPS has “to shame.” *Qll* “be light” is the opposite of *kbd* “be heavy,” the root of *niḵbaddê-ʾāreṣ*: the earth's honored, its “weighty” ones, are made light. The same pair of verbs stands at 8:23. The English cannot keep the wordplay, so it is recorded here. “YHWH of hosts” follows overlay `yhwh-tzevaot-hosts-isaiah`.

paragraphs.translit: YHWH ṣəbāʾōt yəʿāṣāh ləḥallēl gəʾōn kol-ṣəbī ləhāqēl kol-nikbaddē-ʾāreṣ

paragraphs.text: עִבְרִ֥י אַרְצֵ֖ךְ כַּיְאֹ֑ר בַּת־תַּרְשִׁ֕ישׁ אֵ֖ין מֵ֥זַח עֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: Pass through your land like the Nile, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no restraint any more.
i18n.he: עִבְרִ֥י אַרְצֵ֖ךְ כַּיְאֹ֑ר בַּת־תַּרְשִׁ֕ישׁ אֵ֖ין מֵ֥זַח עֽוֹד׃

notes.official:
*ʿIḇrî ʾarṣēḵ kayᵉʾōr baṯ-taršîš ʾên mēzaḥ ʿôḏ* is one of the chapter's cruxes. The line translates MT with ASV: “Pass through your land like the Nile, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no restraint any more.” JPS 1917 has “Overflow thy land as the Nile … there is no girdle any more.” It takes *ʿbr* as the flood spreading over the land and *mēzaḥ* as “girdle” (*mēzaḥ* “belt,” Ps 109:19; compare *mᵉzîaḥ*, Job 12:21; recalled). On that reading the restraint that bound Tarshish to Tyre is gone. NJPS renders “Traverse your land like the Nile, Fair Tarshish; This is a harbor no more.” Its notes say the meaning is uncertain and that *mezaḥ* is taken as a by-form of *māḥôz* “harbor” (Ps 107:30). They add that an emendation yields “Pass on to the land of Kittim, You ships of Tarshish.” NRSV prints a reading of that kind, “Cross over to your own land, O ships of Tarshish; this is a harbor no more” (recalled, not verified). The LXX (Rahlfs) reads ἐργάζου τὴν γῆν σου “work your land,” that is *ʿiḇdî* for *ʿiḇrî*, and goes on “for ships no longer come from Carthage,” its rendering of Tarshish.

The draft also reported that 1QIsaᵃ reads “ships of Tarshish” here. That report is not supported: the online collation of col. XVIII (Miller) lists no variant in this verse and translates “daughter of Tarshish.” The collation was not checked against DJD 32, so the scroll's reading is marked “not verified.” “Ships of Tarshish” is an emendation (the NJPS note says only “Emendation yields”), with partial support in the LXX's “ships” (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *Kayᵉʾōr* is “like the Nile” under the Isaiah context clause of the central `yeor-nile-egyptian-loanword` (see 23:3). *ʾArṣēḵ* is the territorial “land” (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.translit: ʿibrī ʾarṣēk kayʾōr bat-taršīš ʾēn mēzaḥ ʿōd

paragraphs.text: יָדוֹ֙ נָטָ֣ה עַל־הַיָּ֔ם הִרְגִּ֖יז מַמְלָכ֑וֹת יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶל־כְּנַ֔עַן לַשְׁמִ֖ד מָעֻזְנֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: He has stretched out his hand over the sea, he has shaken kingdoms; YHWH has given command concerning Canaan, to destroy its strongholds.
i18n.he: יָדוֹ֙ נָטָ֣ה עַל־הַיָּ֔ם הִרְגִּ֖יז מַמְלָכ֑וֹת יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶל־כְּנַ֔עַן לַשְׁמִ֖ד מָעֻזְנֶֽיהָ׃

notes.official: *Yāḏô nāṭāh ʿal-hayyām* “He has stretched out his hand over the sea” uses the gesture of the outstretched-hand passages (5:25; 9:11; 14:26–27), here over the sea itself. *Kᵉnaʿan* is “Canaan,” with ASV and JPS 1917. Here it denotes the Phoenician coast, which NJPS makes explicit as “Phoenicia's,” with the note “Heb. ‘Canaan’s.’” The identification is given in commentary and kept out of the line. *Māʿuzneyhā* “its strongholds” is an unusual form of *māʿôz* with an inserted *n*. The online collation (Miller) reports a singular form in 1QIsaᵃ, which was not checked against DJD 32 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`).

paragraphs.translit: yādō nāṭāh ʿal-hayyām hirgīz mamlākōt YHWH ṣiwwāh ʾel-kənaʿan lašmid māʿuznēhā

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי ע֖וֹד לַעְל֑וֹז הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָ֞ה בְּתוּלַ֣ת בַּת־צִיד֗וֹן כתיים [כִּתִּים֙] ק֣וּמִי עֲבֹ֔רִי גַּם־שָׁ֖ם לֹא־יָנ֥וּחַֽ לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And he said: “You shall exult no more, O oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon; arise, cross over to Kittim — even there you will have no rest.”
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי ע֖וֹד לַעְל֑וֹז הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָ֞ה בְּתוּלַ֣ת בַּת־צִיד֗וֹן כתיים [כִּתִּים֙] ק֣וּמִי עֲבֹ֔רִי גַּם־שָׁ֖ם לֹא־יָנ֥וּחַֽ לָֽךְ׃

notes.official:
*Lōʾ-ṯôsîp̄î ʿôḏ laʿălôz* “You shall exult no more” uses the infinitive of *ʿlz*, the root of *ʿallîzāh* “jubilant” in 23:7. ASV and JPS 1917 have “rejoice” and NJPS “be gay.” *Hamᵉʿuššāqāh bᵉṯûlaṯ baṯ-ṣîḏôn* “O oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon” is the wording of ASV and JPS 1917. The Pual of *ʿšq* means “oppressed, wronged,” and NJPS has “O plundered one, Fair Maiden Sidon.” *Bᵉṯûlaṯ baṯ-* is a set phrase that personifies a city (“the virgin daughter of Zion,” 37:22; “of Babylon,” 47:1).

The ketiv *כתיים* and the qere *כִּתִּים* differ only in spelling, and the line translates the qere, “Kittim” (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The quotation runs to the end of the verse, as in NJPS. JPS 1917 closes it after “rejoice” and treats the vocative as narration (overlay `title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`). Even flight across the sea to Kittim, usually identified with Cyprus, brings no rest.

paragraphs.translit: wayyōʾmer lōʾ-tōsīpī ʿōd laʿlōz hamʿuššāqāh bətūlat bat-ṣīdōn ktyym [kittīm] qūmī ʿăbōrī gam-šām lōʾ-yānūaḥ lāk

paragraphs.text: הֵ֣ן ׀ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה אַשּׁ֖וּר יְסָדָ֣הּ לְצִיִּ֑ים הֵקִ֣ימוּ בחיניו [בַחוּנָ֗יו] עֹרְרוּ֙ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שָׂמָ֖הּ לְמַפֵּלָֽה׃

i18n.en: Behold, the land of the Chaldeans! This people was not; Assyria founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up his siege towers, they overthrew its palaces; he made it a ruin.
i18n.he: הֵ֣ן ׀ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה אַשּׁ֖וּר יְסָדָ֣הּ לְצִיִּ֑ים הֵקִ֣ימוּ בחיניו [בַחוּנָ֗יו] עֹרְרוּ֙ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שָׂמָ֖הּ לְמַפֵּלָֽה׃

notes.official:
This is the hardest verse in the chapter. MT reads *hēn ʾereṣ kaśdîm zeh hāʿām lōʾ hāyāh ʾaššûr yᵉsāḏāh lᵉṣiyyîm*, and the line follows it with ASV: “Behold, the land of the Chaldeans! This people was not; Assyria founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness.” Read this way, the verse holds up Babylonia as a precedent: a land that Assyria laid waste is a warning to Tyre. Sennacherib's destruction of Babylon in 689 BCE is the event usually cited. JPS 1917 construes the verse differently: “this is the people that was not, when Asshur founded it for shipmen.” NJPS has “This is the people that has ceased to be. Assyria, which founded it for ships …,” with *ṣiyyîm* as “ships” (*ṣî*, Num 24:24; Isa 33:21) and the note “Meaning of verse uncertain.” NRSV repunctuates: “This is the people; it was not Assyria. They destined Tyre for wild animals” (recalled, not verified). Emending *kaśdîm* to *kittîm* gives a verse about Cyprus, and the NJPS note prints a full reconstruction on that basis: “The land of Kittim itself — Which the Sidonian people founded … Exists no more; Assyria has turned it into a ruin.” Many commentators take the verse as a later gloss that turns the oracle toward Babylon (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp; recalled). The line does not decide among these readings.

*Lᵉṣiyyîm* is “for those who dwell in the wilderness,” with ASV. The same form is “desert creatures” at the stable 13:21. The ASV phrase is kept because it leaves open whether people or beasts are meant; on either reading the land is given over to the desert. “Chaldeans” is the book's form (13:19; 43:14; 48:14, 20), and “Assyria” takes the English form (overlay `aram-names-isaiah`). The central `eretz-kasdim` entry (“the land of the Kasdim”), whose scope is Ezekiel, is not applied.

In the second half the ketiv is *bḥynyw* and the qere *baḥûnāyw* “his siege towers,” from a rare noun *baḥûn* / *baḥîn*. The line translates the qere (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). MT shifts number: *hēqîmû* “they set up,” *ʿōrᵉrû* “they overthrew” (Poel of *ʿrr* “lay bare, raze”), *śāmāh* “he made it.” ASV smooths this to “their towers … they made it a ruin,” and JPS 1917 has “their towers … it is made a ruin.” The line keeps the numbers of MT: the Assyrians set up their king's siege towers, and he made the city a ruin. The online collation (Miller) reports feminine singular suffixes in 1QIsaᵃ and a different form for *lᵉṣiyyîm*. This was not checked against DJD 32 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`).

paragraphs.translit: hēn | ʾereṣ kaśdīm zeh hāʿām lōʾ hāyāh ʾaššūr yəsādāh ləṣiyyīm hēqīmū bḥynyw [baḥūnāyw] ʿōrərū ʾarmənōtēhā śāmāh ləmappēlāh

paragraphs.text: הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מָעֻזְּכֶֽן׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste.
i18n.he: הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מָעֻזְּכֶֽן׃ (ס)

notes.official: The verse repeats the summons of 23:1, *hêlîlû ʾŏniyyôṯ taršîš*, and closes the poem. *Māʿuzzᵉḵen* “your stronghold” has a feminine plural suffix, which agrees with *ʾŏniyyôṯ* “ships” (feminine). *Šuddad* is “laid waste,” as in 23:1 (ASV, JPS 1917). A setumah (ס) follows and divides the poem from the prose of 23:15–18 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`).

paragraphs.translit: hēlīlū ʾŏniyyōt taršīš kī šuddad māʿuzzəken (s)

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה כִּימֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶחָ֑ד מִקֵּ֞ץ שִׁבְעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לְצֹ֔ר כְּשִׁירַ֖ת הַזּוֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass in that day that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will be for Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
i18n.he: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה כִּימֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶחָ֑ד מִקֵּ֞ץ שִׁבְעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לְצֹ֔ר כְּשִׁירַ֖ת הַזּוֹנָֽה׃

notes.official:
The prose appendix opens with *wᵉnišḵaḥaṯ ṣōr šiḇʿîm šānāh kîmê meleḵ ʾeḥāḏ* “Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, like the days of one king.” ASV and JPS 1917 have “according to the days of one king,” and NJPS gives the sense: “equaling the lifetime of one king.” The phrase means a lifetime, or the span of a single reign or dynasty. Seventy years is also the length of Babylon's rule in Jer 25:11–12 and 29:10. The central entries for other seventies (Gen 46; Deut 32:8; Dan 9) govern other formulas and are not applied (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`).

*Kᵉšîraṯ hazzônāh* “as in the song of the prostitute” renders *zônāh* as in the central `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus` (“prostitute”), as at 1:21. ASV and JPS 1917 have “harlot.” The verse ends with a colon, and the song follows in quotation marks (overlay `title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`). The online collation (Miller) reports that 1QIsaᵃ leaves out about ten words of this verse; the scribe's eye apparently jumped from one *ṣōr* to the next. This was not checked against DJD 32 (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh bayyōm hahūʾ wəniškaḥat ṣōr šibʿīm šānāh kīmē melek ʾeḥād miqqēṣ šibʿīm šānāh yihyeh ləṣōr kəšīrat hazzōnāh

paragraphs.text: קְחִ֥י כִנּ֛וֹר סֹ֥בִּי עִ֖יר זוֹנָ֣ה נִשְׁכָּחָ֑ה הֵיטִ֤יבִי נַגֵּן֙ הַרְבִּי־שִׁ֔יר לְמַ֖עַן תִּזָּכֵֽרִי׃

i18n.en: “Take a lyre, go about the city, O forgotten prostitute; play skillfully, sing many songs, that you may be remembered.”
i18n.he: קְחִ֥י כִנּ֛וֹר סֹ֥בִּי עִ֖יר זוֹנָ֣ה נִשְׁכָּחָ֑ה הֵיטִ֤יבִי נַגֵּן֙ הַרְבִּי־שִׁ֔יר לְמַ֖עַן תִּזָּכֵֽרִי׃

notes.official: The song is addressed to a woman, in feminine singular imperatives: *qᵉḥî kinnôr sōbbî ʿîr zônāh nišḵāḥāh* “Take a lyre, go about the city, O forgotten prostitute.” *Kinnôr* is “lyre,” as at 5:12 and 24:8, and “harp” stays with *nēḇel* (14:11). ASV and JPS 1917 have “harp,” and NJPS has “lyre.” *Hêṭîḇî naggēn* is literally “do well at playing,” rendered “play skillfully”; ASV and JPS 1917 have “make sweet melody” and NJPS “Sweetly play.” *Lᵉmaʿan tizzāḵērî* “that you may be remembered” answers *nišḵāḥāh* “forgotten” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`). ASV and JPS 1917 print the song without quotation marks, and NJPS sets it as verse. The quotation marks here follow the house style for embedded speech (overlay `title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: qəḥī kinnōr sōbbī ʿīr zōnāh niškāḥāh hēṭībī naggēn harbī-šīr ləmaʿan tizzākērī

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֞ה מִקֵּ֣ץ ׀ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יִפְקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־צֹ֔ר וְשָׁבָ֖ה לְאֶתְנַנָּ֑ה וְזָֽנְתָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass at the end of seventy years that YHWH will visit Tyre, and she will return to her hire and will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֞ה מִקֵּ֣ץ ׀ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יִפְקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־צֹ֔ר וְשָׁבָ֖ה לְאֶתְנַנָּ֑ה וְזָֽנְתָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

notes.official:
*Yip̄qōḏ YHWH ʾeṯ-ṣōr* “YHWH will visit Tyre”: *pqd* means to attend to someone, for good or for ill, and here the sense is restoration. ASV has “visit,” JPS 1917 “remember” and NJPS “take note of.” The line keeps ASV's neutral verb. The overlay entry `yippaqedu-pqd-visitation-imprisonment-isaiah-24` (“punished,” in the judgment of 24:21–22) and the central `paqod-yiphqod-divine-visitation-exodus-formula-cross-corpus` are not applied (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`).

*Wᵉšāḇāh lᵉʾeṯnannāh wᵉzānᵉṯāh* “and she will return to her hire and will prostitute herself”: *ʾeṯnan* is a prostitute's fee (Deut 23:19 Heb., *ʾeṯnan zônāh*; Hos 9:1; Mic 1:7), and the verb is *znh*, the root of *zônāh*. This wave extends the central `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus` to the verb, “prostitute herself,” and to the noun, “hire.” ASV and JPS 1917 have “hire,” and ASV has “play the harlot.” The figure is commercial. NJPS renders “she shall resume her ‘fee-taking’ and ‘play the harlot’,” with the note “I.e., ‘trading…trade’,” and JPS 1917 has “shall have commerce.” *Kol-mamlᵉḵôṯ hāʾāreṣ ʿal-pᵉnê hāʾăḏāmāh* is “all the kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground” (overlay `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`; central `adam-adamah`). ASV and JPS 1917 have “of the world upon the face of the earth.”

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh miqqēṣ | šibʿīm šānāh yipqōd YHWH ʾet-ṣōr wəšābāh ləʾetnannāh wəzānətāh ʾet-kol-mamləkōt hāʾāreṣ ʿal-pənē hāʾădāmāh

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֨ה סַחְרָ֜הּ וְאֶתְנַנָּ֗הּ קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵֽאָצֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יֵֽחָסֵ֑ן כִּ֣י לַיֹּשְׁבִ֞ים לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה סַחְרָ֔הּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְשָׂבְעָ֖ה וְלִמְכַסֶּ֥ה עָתִֽיק׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And her merchandise and her hire will be holiness to YHWH; it will not be stored up nor hoarded, for her merchandise will be for those who dwell before YHWH, to eat their fill, and for durable clothing.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֨ה סַחְרָ֜הּ וְאֶתְנַנָּ֗הּ קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵֽאָצֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יֵֽחָסֵ֑ן כִּ֣י לַיֹּשְׁבִ֞ים לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה סַחְרָ֔הּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְשָׂבְעָ֖ה וְלִמְכַסֶּ֥ה עָתִֽיק׃ (פ)

notes.official:
*Sᵉḥārāh wᵉʾeṯnannāh qōḏeš laYHWH* “her merchandise and her hire will be holiness to YHWH”: *qōḏeš laYHWH* is the inscription on the high priest's gold plate (Exod 28:36; 39:30) and the words of Zech 14:20–21. Here the words are applied to Tyre's earnings. The line keeps the noun with ASV and JPS 1917 (“holiness to the LORD”); NJPS has “shall be consecrated to the LORD.” Deut 23:19 (Heb.) bars a prostitute's fee from the sanctuary, and here such a fee is devoted to YHWH; the commentaries discuss the tension (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-23`; central `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus` for *ʾeṯnan* “hire”).

*Lōʾ yēʾāṣēr wᵉlōʾ yēḥāsēn* is “it will not be stored up nor hoarded” (ASV “treasured nor laid up”). The adjective *ʿāṯîq* in *wᵉlimḵasseh ʿāṯîq* is rare. ASV takes it as “old,” hence long-lasting, and renders “durable clothing.” JPS 1917 “stately clothing” and NJPS “clothe themselves elegantly” take the sense “choice, fine.” The line keeps ASV and records the alternative. *Hayyōšᵉḇîm lip̄nê YHWH* “those who dwell before YHWH” are probably the temple personnel. A petuḥah (פ) closes the chapter.

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh saḥrāh wəʾetnannāh qōdeš laYHWH lōʾ yēʾāṣēr wəlōʾ yēḥāsēn kī layyōšəbīm lipnē YHWH yihyeh saḥrāh leʾĕkōl ləśābəʿāh wəlimkasseh ʿātīq (p)
